intro.author: Unknown. Jewish tradition credits Jeremiah; the writer drew on royal records such as 'the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah' (e.g. 2 Kings 20:20).
intro.written: Completed during the Babylonian exile, after Jehoiachin's release in 561 BC (25:27). 1 and 2 Kings were originally one book.
intro.audience: Israelites in exile in Babylon, trying to understand why Jerusalem and the temple had fallen
intro.setting: The book covers roughly 850 to 561 BC. The northern kingdom of Israel falls to Assyria in 722 BC; Judah survives about 135 years more until Babylon destroys Jerusalem and the temple in 586 BC (some scholars say 587).
intro.purpose: To explain the exile as the result of generations of covenant-breaking, despite repeated warnings from prophets, while keeping a thread of hope alive in David's surviving heir.
intro.bigIdea: God is patient and sends warning after warning, but persistent unfaithfulness ends in exile.

outline.title: Jehu's revolt to the fall of Samaria
